q2.answer: The consumer queries the core DB for active subscriptions matching account_id and event type or '*', then in one service-DB transaction inserts the event and one deliveries row per match, each with a new uuid. UNIQUE (event_id, subscription_id) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING makes a redelivered message a no-op, and the ack happens only after commit.

q6.answer: All of it lives in the service DB deliveries row: status (pending/delivered/dead), attempts, next_attempt_at, last_status, last_error, dead_at and delivered_at. Per-attempt history goes in delivery_attempts.

q7.answer: It waits as a pending row in the service DB deliveries table with next_attempt_at set to now plus the scheduled wait (with about 10% jitter). Workers poll every second and claim rows whose next_attempt_at is due, so the queue plays no part in retries and its 15-minute delay limit does not matter.

q8.answer: The row stays pending with a 60 s lease in next_attempt_at; when it lapses another instance claims it and resends with the same X-Webhook-Id, so the receiver may see a duplicate (at-least-once). The interrupted attempt counts as spent, and a janitor dead-letters rows stuck at attempts>=8 with 'worker lost'. The dead worker's late write, if any, is fenced out by the attempts check.

q9.answer: They are rows in the same deliveries table with status='dead', dead_at and last_status/last_error, kept 14 days and listed by subscription through an index. Replay sets status='pending', attempts=0, next_attempt_at=now() and dead_at=NULL where status='dead', keeping the same delivery id; it returns 409 if the subscription is still disabled.

q11.answer: On a 410 they are dead-lettered in the same service-DB transaction as the triggering delivery, with last_error='subscription_disabled', so they are visible and replayable rather than dropped or sent. For a dashboard-initiated disable, each waiting delivery is dead-lettered with the same reason when its next send starts and the subscription check finds it disabled.
